experiment_data.hypothesis: Constrained decoding channels BCS-related errors into type substitutions, producing a strong BCS-accuracy correlation (ρ ≈ -0.7 to -0.9) on the same batch type sets where unconstrained decoding shows no significant correlation (ρ=-0.14). If confirmed on the same 25 batches, this establishes format dependency as a paired comparison rather than relying on cross-batch-set inference.
experiment_data.notes: Hypothesis falsified: constrained ρ=-0.16 ≈ unconstrained ρ=-0.14 (Fisher z=-0.04, p=0.97). Format does NOT modulate BCS-accuracy correlation. Both Pearson r ≈ -0.45 (significant, outlier-driven) and Spearman ρ ≈ -0.15 (not significant) are virtually identical under both formats. Overall accuracy unchanged (79.5% vs 79.6%). Implication: BCS effect is format-independent — driven by semantic confusability, not forced-choice error channeling.
